_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRE-CLOSE PRUNE. NOTHING REMOVED, AND THE REASON IS A TIMING FACT THAT THE HANDOFF INTO THIS SLOT GOT WRONG. The 15:21 hourly handed this run 'the pruning of the SMCI row once tonight's print has passed'. This run fires at 15:33 and the print is after the 16:00 close, so the print has NOT passed and cannot pass inside this window. Removing the row now would be deleting a catalyst that has not happened, which is the opposite of the error this file guards against. The row stays, both of its numbers were re-struck, and the prune belongs to the 8/12 open - the first run that will see it in the past. The board renders it PASSED overnight and the validator does not warn until two days, so nothing is hidden by leaving it. THE SPOT AND THE STRADDLE WERE RE-PULLED TOGETHER, WITHIN THREE SECONDS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS PASS. Spot goes from Friday's 15:35 bid of 31.70 to a live 31.34 at 19:36:39 UTC; the option quotes are stamped 19:36:32 to 19:36:38 UTC. A spot refreshed on its own would have shrunk the ratio's denominator while leaving a Friday numerator on top of it, making the implied range wrong in the flattering direction - the exact failure this file's comment warns about, and the reason the 15:21 hourly refused to half-refresh it. THE RECORDED STRIKE MOVED FROM 32 TO 31.50 AND THE SERIES IS PUBLISHED ON BOTH SO THE SWITCH CANNOT FLATTER ANYTHING. Spot is 31.34, so 31.50 is the at-the-money strike the rulebook asks for and 32 is 0.66 away. impliedMove now carries the 31.50 straddle at 0.144. On the CONSTANT 32 strike the three readings run 0.142 (8/10 09:45, spot 32.21), 0.137 (8/10 15:35, spot 31.70) and 0.146 (8/11 15:36, spot 31.34) - so the implied move WIDENED by 0.9 points into the print, and that widening is visible because the old strike was quoted alongside the new one rather than replaced by it. Either number gives the same answer. A NOTE ON WHICH STRIKE IS REALLY THE MONEY, because the two tests disagree and the disagreement is small enough to mislead. By distance to spot, 31.50 wins. By delta symmetry, 32 wins: its call is 0.493 against a -0.507 put, nearer to neutral than 31.50's 0.528 / -0.473. That is the forward sitting a little above spot and nothing more; it does not change the refusal, and it is written down so a later run does not rediscover it as a finding. THE REFUSAL IS UNCHANGED, AND IT IS NOW FURTHER FROM CLOSE THAN IT HAS BEEN. An 8% equity stop inside a 14.4% expected move is a stop the event gaps through rather than fills at. 13.7% refused this trade on Friday and 14.4% refuses it harder; the gap between 8 and 14 was never going to be closed by a decimal.

moves.source: Straddle and spot re-pulled live together at 15:36 ET on 8/11 by the pre-close, inside a three-second window. The SMCI 2026-08-14 31.50 call marks 2.215 (2.19 bid / 2.24 ask, 17,091 open interest, delta 0.528) and the 31.50 put marks 2.300 (2.27 bid / 2.33 ask, 735 open interest, delta -0.473), a 4.515 straddle against a live 31.34 bid - 14.4%, recorded here as 0.144. The 32 strike carried by the two earlier readings was quoted in the same window for continuity: call 1.990 (1.97 / 2.01, 3,536 OI, delta 0.493), put 2.600 (2.56 / 2.64, 1,321 OI, delta -0.507), a 4.590 straddle on the same 31.34 spot - 14.6%, against 13.7% at Friday's close and 14.2% on Friday morning. 31.50 is the at-the-money strike at this spot; 32 is retained in the record so the widening is measured on a constant strike rather than across a strike change. Calendar re-verified live at 15:35 against 760 events across 8/11 to 8/15: SMCI 8/11, timing pm, verified true, no actual, estimate 0.88, and still the ONLY watched name reporting inside the window - which is also the check that clears the OKLO position for an overnight hold, since OKLO appears in none of the 760.

branches.cond: An equity entry considered on SMCI before the 8/11 close
branches.act: Refused, for the last time this branch is reachable - the close is twenty-odd minutes out
branches.why: Item 3 is satisfied by a straddle struck at the same instant as the spot it is divided by, and it decides against the trade rather than merely permitting it to be considered. A 14.4% implied move against the rulebook's -8% equity stop means the stop sits entirely inside the event: the realistic bad case gaps through it rather than filling at it, so the exit written before entry would not be the exit taken. The readings ran 14.2%, then 13.7%, now 14.4%, and the refusal never depended on which of the three it was. This is a mechanical refusal and not a view on whether the report is good.

branches.cond: An option considered on this name at any time before the print
branches.act: Refused outright, and it was never reachable
branches.why: The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print - IV crush kills even a correct call - and any 3-6 week expiry from here necessarily spans 8/11. The straddle does not enter into it; this branch closes on the calendar alone, re-verified live at 15:35. The 8/14 contracts quoted above are the straddle used to price the event and are not themselves proposable: three days to expiry is inside the three-week floor several times over.

branches.cond: SMCI still wanted after the print
branches.act: Re-approach from 8/12, on the reaction bar rather than into it
branches.why: The post-print session is the first point at which this name is available to the rulebook at all, and item 2 will then govern: the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2/3 pullback that holds is. Recorded before the print rather than after it, so a post-print entry is a decision made in advance and a post-print pass is one too. The 8/12 open owns this branch and owns pruning the row above it.
